To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) vitamin A deprivation led to an increase of the oligonucleotides in the testes and mucosa of rats and (2) retinyl acetatesupplementation reversed these effects, whereas retinoate was ineffective in the testis.
vitamin A deficiency caused an increase in the polyadenylic acid content of the intestinal mucosa and a decrease in the charging capacity and poly(A) content of the testes of rats.

vitamin A deficiency led to a decrease in the ribonucleotide content of the testes rRNA and tRNAs, but not in that of the liver rRNA or tRNA; the ribonucleotides of the intestinal mucosa were not affected by vitamin A deficiency; supplementation with retinyl acetatereversed all these effects; supplementation with retinoic acetate was equally effective in the intestinal mucosa, but virtually ineffective in testes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of vitamin A deficiency on the ribonuclease, poly(A) and tRNA acceptor activity of liver, intestinal and testicular tissue of rats and the effect of retinyl acetates and retinoic acid on these parameters.
the effect of vitamin A deficiency on the ribonucelic acids (RNAs) and transfer RNAs (tRNAs) of rat tissues and the reversal of the effects by retinyl and retinoic acid.
the effect of vitamin A deficiency on the ribonucletic acid metabolism of the rat testes and intestinal mucus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of vitamin A deficiency on the testes and mucosa are qualitatively similar, whereas the effects on the liver are different.
the effect of vitamin A deficiency on the testicular RNA is much more pronounced than that of the mucosal RNA and the liver RNA.
vitamin A deprivation leads to a marked decrease in RNA and tRNA synthesis, and that this effect is reversed by retinyl ester supplementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of vitamin A deficiency on the RNA of the testes, intestinal mucosa, and liver is tissue specific.

the effect of vitamin A on the ribonucletic acids of liver and intestinal mucosa is similar to that of the retinyl ester, whereas the effect of the alcohol on the ribonulcetic acids of the testes is similar to that on the intestinal mucosa.

vitamin A deprivation led to an increase of oligonucleotides in the testes and the intestinal mucosa of the rat, whereas retinyl acetatesupplementation reversed the changes, and retinoic acid had a partial effect in this respect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of vitamin A deficiency on RNA metabolism is tissue-specific and that the effect of retinoic acid is less pronounced than that of retinyl acetates.
vitamin A deprivation affects the ribonucleotide metabolism and poly(A) contents in the liver, intestinal mucosal, and testes of growing rats.

the vitamin A deficiency affects the RNA metabolism in testes and intestinal epithelium, which is not observed in the liver, and the retinyl esters are more effective than retinoic acid in reversing the vitamin A-deficiency effects.
